description: Saves an issue (the essays in order, the title, the artist in residence and the works for its plates) and returns a short link to a page where it is already laid out as a stapled 8.5 x 11 in print magazine: cover art, contents, each essay set in print type, a frontispiece, full-page plates on spare pages and white-on-black stencils where an essay ends early, with 'Artist in residence: <name>' on the back cover. The page pages through like the printed copy and takes the order (quantity, then Stripe checkout); copies are printed and shipped to one address, or mailed to a list of the writer's readers. Every work is re-checked against the museum's public-domain flag; anything not flagged, or not by the named artist, is dropped. work_ids are optional: without them, or when too few are given for the plate slots, the artist's sharpest public-domain works fill the rest. Returns the link, the estimated page count, the essays it found, the works on hand and example prices. Example: {"substack":"aidanjude","post_slugs":["oct-26-pt1","oct-26-pt2"],"artist":"Albrecht Dürer","title":"Periodicals","work_ids":["aic:51498","aic:55330"]}.

artist.description: The artist in residence the writer picked

cover_work_id.description: Optional: the work for the front cover

post_slugs.description: The essays, in reading order, by slug

substack.description: Substack handle, subdomain or custom domain

title.description: The magazine's name on the cover (default: the publication's name)

work_ids.description: Optional: works from find_artist_works in order of preference (aic:NNN / cma:NNN); the first portrait one that prints full page sharp is the cover unless cover_work_id is given

name: lay_out_issue
title: Lay out the issue and get a link to the printed magazine, ready to order
